facts.text: The project description is training a humanoid robot for locomotion using reinforcement learning
The declared simulation dependencies are dm-control>=1.0.24 and mujoco==3.4.0
The repository layout labels envs/common/mujoco_env.py as the MuJoCo simulation wrapper and models/ as the MuJoCo model files
MujocoEnv is the superclass for all MuJoCo environments
MujocoEnv refuses a relative model path, opens the model with mujoco.MjSpec.from_file, compiles it and creates the mujoco.MjData it owns
MujocoEnv.reset restores the data with mujoco.mj_resetData and returns the subclass's reset_model observation
BaseHumanoidEnv is the shared humanoid environment base on top of MujocoEnv
BaseHumanoidEnv.step smooths the policy action, runs robot.step and returns the observation, the summed reward, done and the reward dictionary
JvrcWalkEnv is the concrete JVRC walking environment and builds its XML through the jvrc builder
The jvrc builder loads its MJCF from models/jvrc_mj_description/xml/scene.xml
The jvrc builder removes every motor whose joint is not listed in LEG_JOINTS
The served MJCF scene is named 'jvrc1 scene' and includes jvrc1.xml
The model compiles angles in radians and resolves meshes from ../meshes
The model sets option timestep 0.001 s, 50 iterations, the Newton solver, a dense Jacobian and pyramidal friction cones
The default motor class sets ctrllimited="false" and forcelimited="false"
The root body PELVIS_S is placed at 0 0 1.4 and carries the free joint root
The R_HIP_P hinge has range -2.0944 to 0.785398 rad and armature 0.1925
The L_KNEE hinge has range 0 to 2.61799 rad and armature 0.1305
The actuator section has one motor for each leg, waist, neck, arm and thumb joint and no motor for the distal finger joints
Ten equality constraints couple the five distal finger joints of each hand to its thumb
The sensor section reads force and torque at both feet and both hands and a gyro and accelerometer at the imu site
H1Env is a Unitree H1 standing environment
The JVRC model submodule's LICENSE states BSD 2-Clause

determinism.notes: the fake uses fixed model defaults and deterministic placeholder updates; no RNG or MuJoCo trajectory comparison is involved

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the MJCF (scene.xml includes jvrc1.xml) for the joint layout, the actuator targets and the option timestep, but integrates a placeholder acceleration from each motor control, using distinct qpos/qvel addresses and the model's default floating-base pose; it has no mass matrix, damping or coupled dynamics, so trajectories, contacts, actuator dynamics and the free-base dynamics are not MuJoCo's

the model's motors set ctrllimited=false and forcelimited=false (xml/jvrc1.xml:13) and declare no ctrlrange (xml/jvrc1.xml:451-492), so the bridge publishes action.ctrl operator_required: a step that sets it is refused until the site's site-limits.json bounds it, and site-limits.example.json is operator example data, not a model bound
no mesh or texture is loaded and no contact, equality, tendon or sensor is resolved by the stand-in; the ten finger equality constraints of xml/jvrc1.xml:436-448 are not applied

the upstream environment layer is NOT COVERED: JvrcWalkEnv's reduced XML (built by envs/jvrc/gen_xml.py from this scene), its action smoothing, PD control, clock and mode observations, rewards and termination are not modelled; this driver serves the raw MJCF control vector of the card's models[0], not the environment's policy action
H1Env (envs/h1/h1_env.py:11-12) and the other environment tasks are not served; the selected device is only the raw JVRC1 scene, whose model submodule has its own BSD-2-Clause LICENSE
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine or with the upstream environment
no rendering is offered and no physical JVRC1 robot is modelled; nothing was validated against hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
